lines.trans: I called her and she says she's crossing Mapo Bridge right now.
She's crossing that bridge every single day!
Wait, why are you buying us Korean beef? That's suspicious.
Are we getting cancelled?
It's not a cancellation, they told us to replace the cast.
Please don't make us do the work twice, I'm dead tired.

words.gram: auxiliary verb, -지 말다 (negative imperative), polite (-아요, contracted)

lines.trans: Is it certain that we writers are staying on?
Who says you're getting cut? Am I that kind of person?

lines.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: Used with -에 or -한테/에게 for the person called.

examples.trans: I'll call you back later.
I called my friend yesterday.

meanings.note: Functions as both an adverb and a noun.

examples.trans: Where are you right now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: A major bridge crossing the Han River in Seoul, connecting Mapo-gu and Yeouido (home to KBS).

examples.trans: Once you cross Mapo Bridge, you're in Yeouido.
Mapo Bridge is very congested during rush hour.

meanings.note: Takes -을/를 for the place being crossed.

examples.trans: Please cross the street carefully.
Right after you cross the bridge, the station appears.

meanings.en: to be, to exist, to stay (honorific of 있다)
meanings.note: Used for respected subjects.

meanings.en: to be doing (honorific progressive auxiliary in -고 계시다)
meanings.note: Replaces -고 있다 when the subject is honored.

examples.trans: Is the teacher in the classroom right now?
Grandmother is sleeping.

meanings.note: Colloquial pronunciation/spelling of 만날; often carries a complaining or emphatic tone.

examples.trans: Why do you come late every day?
These days I work overtime every single day.

meanings.note: Refers to a place near the listener or already mentioned in conversation.

examples.trans: How is the weather there?
Please sit there for just a moment.

있다.gloss: to be, to exist, to have

meanings.en: to be, to exist, to be located
meanings.note: Pairs with -에 for location.

meanings.en: to be doing (progressive auxiliary in -고 있다)
meanings.note: Expresses an ongoing action.

examples.trans: There is coffee on the desk.
I am eating lunch right now.

related.gloss: to not be, to not have

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of 그런데; used to shift topics or raise a question.

examples.trans: By the way, what time are we meeting?
It is delicious, but it's a bit expensive.

meanings.note: Used instead of 우리 when speaking politely to someone of higher status or outside one's group.

examples.trans: Our team presents tomorrow.
Please leave it to us.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb or at the start of a question.

examples.trans: Why is it so quiet today?
Why aren't you saying anything?

meanings.note: Prized, expensive domestic beef often eaten on special occasions or company dinners.

examples.trans: Today's company dinner menu is Korean beef.
Korean beef is expensive, but it's really tender.

meanings.note: Often combined with -아/어 주다 (사주다) to mean 'buy for someone'.

examples.trans: I bought fruit at the supermarket.
I'll buy you coffee today.

meanings.note: Describes something unusual or out of the ordinary.
Used when sensing something is wrong.

examples.trans: The computer sounds a bit strange.
It's suspicious that he's suddenly being so nice.

meanings.note: Also used for things belonging to one's group, family, or workplace (e.g., 우리 회사 'my/our company').

examples.trans: Shall we eat lunch together tomorrow?
My/our house is close to the station.

meanings.en: to disappear, to vanish, to go missing
meanings.note: Intransitive/passive counterpart of 없애다.

meanings.en: to be abolished, to be cancelled (of a program or rule)
meanings.note: Commonly used in broadcasting for a show getting axed.

examples.trans: My wallet suddenly disappeared.
They say that show is getting cancelled this month.

related.gloss: to come into being, to appear

meanings.en: abolition, repeal, cancellation (of a program, system, or law)
meanings.note: Often used with 되다 (폐지되다) or 하다 (폐지하다).

examples.trans: This system will be abolished starting next year.
Because ratings were low, the show's cancellation was decided.

meanings.note: Takes -이/가 before 아니다 (e.g., 학생이 아니다).

examples.trans: I am not on duty today.
That wasn't my fault.

meanings.en: member (of a group, team, or cast)
meanings.note: Loanword from English 'member'.

examples.trans: All the members of our team have gathered.
A new member is joining starting next week.

meanings.en: to replace, to change, to substitute (a person or part)
meanings.note: Used for cast members, players, batteries, etc.

examples.trans: I replaced the battery with a new one.
The coach substituted a player in the second half.

meanings.note: Refers to duties or labor.
Used in expressions like 무슨 일이에요? ('What's the matter?').

examples.trans: I have a lot of work to do today.

examples.text: 무슨 일 있어요? 표정이 안 좋아요.
examples.trans: Is something wrong? You don't look well.

meanings.note: Makes a request or complaint sound less blunt.
Contraction of 조금.

examples.trans: Could you please open the window?
The weather is a bit cold today.

meanings.note: Used before counters and nouns (e.g., 두 번 'twice', 두 명 'two people').

examples.trans: Two cups of coffee, please.
I exercise twice a week.

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

meanings.en: to make someone do, to assign work
meanings.note: Causative verb; e.g., 일을 시키다 'to assign work'.
E.g., 치킨을 시키다 'to order fried chicken'.

examples.trans: The team leader assigned this work to me.
Shall we order pizza for dinner?

meanings.en: to not do (negative imperative/propositive auxiliary in -지 말다)
meanings.note: Used after verb stem + -지 to form 'don't ...' (e.g., 가지 마요).

examples.trans: Please don't worry too much.
Don't park here.

meanings.note: Describes physical or mental tiredness.

examples.text: 어제 잠을 못 자서 너무 피곤해요.
examples.trans: I couldn't sleep yesterday, so I'm really tired.
If you're tired, please rest a bit.

meanings.note: Literal meaning.

meanings.en: to be ... to death (idiomatic in -아/어 죽겠다)
meanings.note: Expresses an extreme feeling, like 배고파 죽겠다 ('starving to death').

examples.text: 추워 죽겠어요, 문 좀 닫아 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm freezing to death, please close the door.
I'm starving to death—shall we eat something?

meanings.note: Basic motion verb away from the speaker.
Used figuratively for continuing in a role or relationship.

examples.trans: I'm going to Seoul Station tomorrow.
Goodbye, see you tomorrow!

meanings.en: thing, fact, one (colloquial contraction of 것)
meanings.note: Used after modifiers (-는 거, -을 거) to nominalize a verb clause.

examples.trans: Is what you're eating right now delicious?
Is it true that it's raining tomorrow?

맞다.gloss: to be right, to be correct

meanings.note: Used to confirm facts or answers.

meanings.en: to fit, to suit, to match
meanings.note: E.g., 사이즈가 맞다 ('the size fits').

examples.trans: Yes, that's my phone number.
These shoes fit my feet perfectly.

meanings.note: Becomes 누가 when combined with the subject particle -가.

examples.trans: Who made this cake?
Who did you eat with yesterday?

meanings.note: Colloquial spoken form of 너희네; used among close friends or to juniors.

examples.text: 너네 오늘 수업 몇 시에 끝나?
examples.trans: What time does your class end today?
You guys all come over here together.

잘리다.gloss: to be cut, to get fired

meanings.en: to be cut, to be severed
meanings.note: Passive of 자르다 ('to cut').

meanings.en: to get fired, to be laid off
meanings.note: Everyday colloquialism for losing one's job.

examples.trans: I'm worried I might get fired from the company.
That scene got cut in editing.

meanings.note: Becomes 내가 before the subject particle -가.

examples.trans: I'll contact you again tomorrow.
I want to watch that movie too.

meanings.en: such, that kind of, like that
meanings.note: Modifier placed directly before a noun.

examples.trans: Please don't say that kind of thing.
I want to become that kind of person too.

meanings.note: General noun for a person.

examples.trans: That person is really kind.
There are many people in the park on weekends.

meanings.note: Used in standard polite greetings such as 안녕히 가세요 ('Goodbye' to someone leaving) and 안녕히 계세요 ('Goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye, get home safely.
Goodbye, I'll be heading out first.
